answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it may bid for work, then slash that stake when a randomly audited task fails or linked accounts coordinate fraud. This makes a sybil attack costly: splitting one agent into many identities multiplies the capital at risk without multiplying the attacker’s resources. A ridge of independent reviewers can verify sampled outputs, while opal and glacier name two audit cohorts whose overlap helps catch collusion.
